title: Load Sculpting and Fidelity Certification Framework
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Load Sculpting and Fidelity Certification Framework (LSFCF): a cross-team protocol and artifact set for validating runtime behavior, kernel scheduler interactions, and model fidelity under sculpted production-like load. The goal is to provide a reproducible, auditable path to certify that a runtime/kernel change or model variant meets latency, cost, and quality gates before rollout to hosted or dedicated fleets.

Scope
-----
Applies to: runtime engineers, kernel/scheduler teams, profiling and benchmarking engineers, QA, and release owners.
Includes artifacts: load sculpting profiles, fidelity acceptance tests, end-to-end scenario harnesses, release-checklist items, and a minimal certification report template.
Excludes: model training/eval-only artifacts (handled by applied-ml-and-evals).

Motivation
----------
We frequently observe subtle regressions that only surface when the scheduler interacts with specific request shapes (eg. many short queries with heavy KV-cache churn, or large context continuations causing kernel fallback). The LSFCF standardizes how we: 
- Compose sculpted traffic that stresses critical kernel/scheduling paths.
- Correlate profiling signals (kernel latency, SM occupancy, memory pressure) with end-to-end SLOs and model-quality regressions.
- Produce a certification record with deterministic criteria for progressive rollouts.

Definitions
-----------
- Sculpted profile: synthetic traffic pattern derived from production traces and parameterized by QPS, concurrency, sequence-length distribution, and session affinity.
- Fidelity gate: a threshold-based test comparing model output on a canonical prompt set, measured by quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity/regression-count).
- Certification run: full execution of LSFCF artifacts across target hardware and runtime configurations; includes profiling capture and post-run analysis.

Framework overview
------------------
1) Selection: Identify target dimensions to exercise: sequence length tail, KV-cache churn, batch shape skew, priority churn, and mixed tenant interference.
2) Build sculpted profile: parameterize generator with distribution seeds, warmup/cooldown windows, and correlated metadata (token budgets, prompt templates, tool-calls).
3) Execute harness across three fidelity lanes:
   - Canary-lab: single-node variant to validate functional correctness and basic perf.
   - Integration-stable: 10–50 node cluster with representative scheduler configuration and simulated multi-tenant noise.
   - Preprod-mirror: traffic-mirroring of a sampled production window with 10–20% production QPS (read-only for data plane).
4) Capture telemetry: kernel traces, per-kernel histogram, GPU occupancy, allocator metrics, RPC latencies, and request provenance.
5) Run fidelity tests: prompt-set pass/fail and quality delta thresholds.
6) Produce a certification report with pass/fail verdicts, regression vectors, and rollout recommendation.

Sculpted profiles (example table)
--------------------------------
| profile_name | qps_peak | concurrency | seq_len_p95 | kv_churn_rate | notes |
|---------------|---------:|------------:|-----------:|--------------:|-------|
| short-burst-sprint | 1200 | 400 | 32 | high | Many small requests, spikes every 30s |
| long-stream-continuous | 200 | 40 | 2048 | low | Streaming dominated, long KV retention |
| mixed-tenant-noise | 600 | 250 | 128 | medium | 60/40 mix of short and long sessions |
| tool-call-heavy | 80 | 20 | 512 | high | Frequent function/tool invocation latencies matter |

Execution procedure (step-by-step)
---------------------------------
1. Approve test matrix with product/release owner and SRE. Include hardware SKUs and quantization profile.
2. Checkout the runtime commit/tag and kernel rollout candidate.
3. Provision harness cluster: specify node count and scheduler flags. Example CLI:
   
   ./harness/provision --profile short-burst-sprint --nodes 25 --scheduler-flags "preemptive_shepherding=true,kv_prefetch=adaptive"

4. Deploy canary binary and model variant to canary-lab. Run basic smoke tests.
5. Start sculpted traffic with deterministic seed and run for baseline window (recommended 30m warmup + 60m measurement). CLI example:
   
   ./harness/run --seed 42 --duration 90m --capture-traces --output /tmp/lsfcf-run-2028-02-01

6. Collect artifacts: kernel-trace.pb, telemetry-rollup.json, fidelity-diffs.json, and perf-summaries.csv. Upload to run artifact store.
7. Run automated analysis job (analysis-runner) to compute SLO deltas and kernel-sensitivity indices.

Profiling and observability integration
-------------------------------------
- Required traces: per-kernel timestamped spans, CUDA kernel labels, post-dispatch occupancy summaries, per-request decision trace.
- Metrics to compute: per-kernel p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel invocation rate per second, eviction rate, allocator fragmentation ratio, RPC retry counts.
- Tagging: every event must include run_id, profile_name, runtime_commit, model_version, and node_affinity.
- Visualization: use the runtime perf dashboard with the LSFCF panel (panels: kernel-sensitivity heatmap, fidelity-delta trend, occupancy timeline).

Fidelity testing (canonical prompt set)
-------------------------------------
- Prompt set: 500 prompts representing core downstream intents (generated from product telemetry and curated to surface hallucination cases).
- Success criteria: mean embedding-similarity decline <= 0.015 vs baseline and no more than 6% increased regression alerts on intent-critical prompts.
- If fidelity fails: abort certification and follow triage section below.

Kernel scheduling checks and hints
--------------------------------
Before certification, execute the kernel-scheduler sanity script which validates mapping between request priority and kernel credit windows. Example checks:
- No kernel preemption storms (more than 5 preempts/sec/node for longer than 60s).
- Eviction churn < 0.8 evictions/sec/KB of active KV cache.
- Batch-slice size variance within expected tolerance (target variance < 25%).

Sample kernel-sanity command:

./tools/kernel-sanity --run-id $RUN_ID --expectations expectations.yaml --output sanity-report.json

Triage runbook (if a run fails)
------------------------------
1. Immediate actions (first 30 minutes):
   a. Stop progressive rollout if one is active.
   b. Collect most recent artifacts and tag run as FAILED in the artifact store.
   c. Page runtime-oncall and kernel-owner channels.
2. Short investigation (30–180 minutes):
   a. Run kernel-level replicator on a single affected node with the same sculpted input seed.
   b. Compare baseline kernel histograms with candidate. Compute kernel-sensitivity index and list top-3 divergent kernels.
   c. If a single kernel is responsible, attempt revert/patch and run targeted microbenchmark.
3. Root cause and remediation (post-incident):
   a. Produce an incident note with a causal chain and decision.
   b. If regression is from scheduler policy, update scheduler policy matrix and add a new unit test in kernel integration tests.

Certification report (required fields)
------------------------------------
- run_id
- profile_name
- runtime_commit
- kernel_tag
- model_version
- hardware_skus
- summary_pass_fail (PASS/FAIL)
- per-metric deltas (latency, cost/token, fidelity)
- top divergent kernels (by invocation/time)
- recommended rollout path (canary -> phased -> full or blocked)
- owner and approver signatures

Release checklist (pre-rollout)
------------------------------
- [ ] Certification report present and PASS
- [ ] Oncall briefed and escalation contact verified
- [ ] Fallback variant verified (known-good model or lower-capacity runtime)
- [ ] Canary config defined (percentage progression and hold times)
- [ ] Monitoring alerts tuned for new kernel labels

Known limitations and current issues
----------------------------------
- Tooling gap: cross-node GPU trace stitching is approximate when nodes have clock skew > 2s; we annotate such runs as "clock-skew-approx".
- Measurement noise: mixed-tenant runs can exhibit >5% variance for p99 in low-sample windows; use 60m measurement window when possible.
- Coverage: the LSFCF currently does not emulate PCIe/host-memory bandwidth saturation; schedule a separate IO-stress suite for those checks.

Ownership and run cadence
------------------------
- Owners: eng-serving-runtime (lead: Aisha Patel), kernel-scheduler team (reviewer: Marco Ruiz), profiling (reviewer: Lena Thompson).
- Cadence: Every runtime or kernel PR that touches scheduler/kernel code must have at least one full LSFCF canary-lab run. Major releases require Integration-stable and Preprod-mirror runs.

Artifacts and storage layout
--------------------------
Artifacts are stored under: s3://runtime-artifacts/lsfcf/{year}/{run_id}/
Required files: kernel-trace.pb, telemetry-rollup.json, fidelity-diffs.json, perf-summaries.csv, certification-report.yaml

Appendix A: expectations.yaml (recommended minimal)
--------------------------------------------------
| metric | pass_threshold | warning_threshold | notes |
|--------|---------------:|------------------:|-------|
| p95_e2e_latency | <= 180ms | <= 220ms | measured across measurement window |
| cost_per_1k_tokens | <= +8% | <= +12% | compared to baseline run |
| fidelity_embedding_delta | <= 0.015 | <= 0.025 | mean cosine distance |
| eviction_churn | <= 0.8 evictions/sec/KB | <= 1.2 | higher indicates instability |

Appendix B: example CI integration snippet
-----------------------------------------
- job: lsfcf-canary
  script:
    - ./harness/provision --profile short-burst-sprint --nodes 10 --scheduler-flags "preemptive_shepherding=true"
    - ./harness/run --seed $CI_RUN_SEED --duration 90m --capture-traces --output /tmp/lsfcf-ci
    - ./analysis/runner --input /tmp/lsfcf-ci --expectations expectations.yaml --output /tmp/lsfcf-ci/summary.json
  artifacts:
    - /tmp/lsfcf-ci/**

Appendix C: contacts and escalation
----------------------------------
- Runtime oncall: #eng-runtime-oncall
- Kernel scheduler owner: marco.ruiz@redwood.ai
- Profiling lead: lena.thompson@redwood.ai
